answer: Transitive trust graphs curb Sybil attacks by routing reputation along verified paths from seed nodes. Agents sign interaction receipts with an asymmetric cipher to build peer edges. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of securing honest attestations per identity, rendering mass cloning an economic fable. Cut analysis acts as an audit lantern to isolate dense bot clusters. However, compromised bridge nodes can leak trust to malicious subgraphs, while newcomers suffer cold-start friction.
